lit-cl-01-c4.text: Milman Parry (1930). Studies in the Epic Technique of Oral Verse-Making: I. Homer and Homeric Style. Harvard Studies in Classical Philology 41 (hosted by the Center for Hellenic Studies, Harvard).
lit-cl-01-c4.quote: Parry defines the formula as "a group of words which is regularly employed under the same metrical conditions to express a given essential idea" (p. 80).
lit-cl-01-c4.claim: Performers used formulaic phrases ('rosy-fingered dawn,' 'wine-dark sea,' 'swift-footed Achilles') that fit specific metrical positions.

lit-cl-02-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2015). Aeschylus. World History Encyclopedia.
lit-cl-02-c1.quote: 5th century BCE Athens was blessed with three great tragedians: Aeschylus, Euripides (c. 484 - 407 BCE), and Sophocles (c. 496 - c. 406 BCE).
lit-cl-02-c1.claim: Three poets dominate the surviving record: Aeschylus, Sophocles, Euripides.

lit-cl-02-c4.text: Mark Cartwright (2015). Euripides. World History Encyclopedia.
lit-cl-02-c4.quote: Medeia (431 BCE) - where Jason, of the Golden Fleece fame, abandons the title character for the daughter of the King of Corinth with the consequence that Medeia kills her own children in revenge.
lit-cl-02-c4.claim: Medea (431 BCE) shows a wronged woman taking vengeance by killing her own children.

lit-cl-04-c3.text: Donald L. Wasson (2017). Ovid. World History Encyclopedia.
lit-cl-04-c3.quote: Metamorphoses, 15 books composed in dactylic hexameter, a collection of tales garnered from classical and Near Eastern myths and legends
lit-cl-04-c3.claim: His Metamorphoses is a sprawling 15-book epic of mythological transformations: gods, mortals, and creatures changing shape.

lit-cl-03-c1.quote: eleven comic plays survive, and they are the only examples of the so-called Old Comic style
lit-cl-03-c1.claim: Aristophanes (c. 446-386 BCE) is the only major Old Comic poet whose plays survive. Eleven plays remain.

lit-cl-05-c2.quote: Petrarch actively searched for 'lost' ancient manuscripts hidden away in forgotten corners of medieval libraries
lit-cl-05-c2.claim: Petrarch hunted down lost Latin manuscripts and built a humanist library.

lit-cl-05-c3.text: John Milton (1667). Paradise Lost, Book I. Project Gutenberg.
lit-cl-05-c3.quote: though all the giant brood Of Phlegra with th’ heroic race were joined That fought at Thebes and Ilium, on each side Mixed with auxiliar gods
lit-cl-05-c3.claim: he compares it to 'the heroic race ... that fought at Thebes and Ilium'
